name: Beta-thalassemia and Related Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of microcytic hypochromic anemia with low mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH)
Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing reduced or absent HbA with increased HbA2 and/or HbF
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the HBB gene by molecular genetic testing
Clinical features such as pallor, jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, and growth retardation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of microcytic anemia plus confirmatory hemoglobin electrophoresis or genetic testing identifying HBB mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may require combination of hematological, biochemical, and genetic tests.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic anemia with low MCV and MCH
searchTerms: anemia with small, light-colored red cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated HbA2 and/or HbF levels on hemoglobin electrophoresis
searchTerms: high HbA2 or HbF on blood test

pathognomonic.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to extramedullary hematopoiesis

searchTerms: yellow skin from red blood cell breakdown

common.symptomName: Bone deformities including frontal bossing and maxillary overgrowth
searchTerms: abnormal skull and facial bone shape

occasional.symptomName: Iron overload complications (cardiac arrhythmias, liver fibrosis)
searchTerms: iron overload causing heart and liver problems
cardiac arrhythmias and liver fibrosis due to iron
blood cell production outside bone marrow

occasional.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction including hypothyroidism and diabetes mellitus
searchTerms: hormone problems like hypothyroidism and diabetes
endocrine dysfunction with thyroid and sugar issues

rare.symptomName: Cognitive impairment secondary to chronic anemia
searchTerms: thinking problems due to chronic anemia
cognitive impairment from low blood count

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with low MCV and MCH
Elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation (iron overload)
Elevated HbA2 and HbF on hemoglobin electrophoresis
imaging: Skull X-ray showing 'hair-on-end' appearance due to marrow expansion
MRI for iron overload quantification in liver and heart
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in the HBB gene detected by molecular genetic testing

distinguishingFeatures: Different hemoglobin electrophoresis pattern with decreased HbA and HbH inclusion bodies
More common in Southeast Asian populations
Low serum ferritin and iron levels
No elevation of HbA2 or HbF on electrophoresis
Presence of ring sideroblasts in bone marrow

redFlags: Severe anemia requiring regular blood transfusions
Signs of iron overload such as cardiac dysfunction or liver fibrosis
Marked bone deformities and growth retardation
references: Cappellini MD, Cohen A, Porter J, Taher A, Viprakasit V. Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion Dependent Thalassaemia (TDT). 3rd Edition. Thalassaemia International Federation; 2014.
